title: PIN-01 AC4: PinResolver.applyPinOverrides() stores a JSON-parser-owned string pointer into PinnedVersion.version, causing a double-free (Invalid free panic) on the valid-override success path
summary: Independently re-running `zig build test-integration-pin01` (against real PostgreSQL, BPM_TEST_DB_URL from .env) during TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's Step 3b verification pass showed 8 pass, 1 crash (9 total) -- not the clean all-green result the routing handoff described. TC-PIN-01-03 ('resolve applies a valid pin_overrides entry, source becomes override') crashes the test binary with a Zig DebugAllocator 'Invalid free' panic at src/engine/pin_resolver.zig:195 (allocator.free(src.version) inside resolve()'s Step 6 success-path cleanup loop). Root cause: applyPinOverrides() (pin_resolver.zig ~line 458) parses pin_overrides JSON with std.json.parseFromSlice(..., allocator, ...) and reads the override's version field via jsonStringField(), which returns a slice pointing directly into the parsed JSON value's own storage (owned by `parsed`, freed by applyPinOverrides()'s own `defer parsed.deinit()` on return). For the catalog_entry branch, when an override matches, applyOverrideToPins() (line 533) stores that JSON-parser-owned slice directly into p.version -- a pointer that dangles the instant applyPinOverrides() returns. resolve()'s Step 6 cleanup loop (line 170-196) then unconditionally calls allocator.free(src.version) on every pin, assuming every .version is always allocator-owned (true for the non-override path) -- for an overridden pin this frees memory std.json's parser already freed, a genuine double-free that Zig's DebugAllocator catches as 'Invalid free' and panics the process. This reproduces deterministically on every resolve() call where a pin_overrides entry successfully matches and applies -- i.e. PIN-01 AC4's accepting/happy path, not an edge case. The variable_schema override branch (line 513-526) has the identical pattern (version is again the JSON-parser-owned slice passed into applyOverrideToPins).

root_cause.details: applyOverrideToPins() stores a string slice owned by a short-lived std.json ParseResult (freed by applyPinOverrides()'s defer parsed.deinit()) directly into a long-lived PinnedVersion.version field that resolve()'s Step 6 cleanup loop later frees via the caller-supplied `allocator`, on the (here-false) assumption that all PinnedVersion string fields are always allocator-owned. The pointer is valid at the moment of assignment but dangles by the time resolve() reaches its cleanup loop, and freeing already-freed memory corrupts the DebugAllocator's bucket canary.

resolution.details: src/engine/pin_resolver.zig: applyOverrideToPins() now takes the allocator, allocator.dupe()s the incoming resolved_id/version before storing into the pin, and frees the pin's OLD resolved_id/version before overwriting -- mirroring the dupe-then-free pattern resolve()'s own Step 6 success-path loop already uses for the non-override path. At both applyPinOverrides() call sites (catalog_entry branch ~line 501-520, variable_schema branch ~line 522-543), the resolved.resolved_id/.version and current.resolved_id/.version returned by resolveServiceCatalogRef()/resolveVariableSchemaVersion() are now unconditionally freed by the CALLER via defer (both are always allocator-owned per those functions' own contract), regardless of whether the override matches -- applyOverrideToPins() takes its own independent dupe rather than aliasing the caller's copy, so the two frees can never collide.

verification: zig build test-integration-pin01 run twice (2 separate foreground invocations, different random seeds 0xc560c37 and a second distinct seed): both runs report 9 pass (9 total), 0 crashes, 0 "Invalid free" panics -- identical result both times. TC-PIN-01-03 (the AC4 override success path that was crashing) now passes cleanly. zig build / zig build check / zig build test all exit 0 with no regressions. NOTE: 8 pre-existing memory leaks remain in TC-PIN-01-02 and TC-PIN-01-04 (both error-return paths) -- these are the separately tracked, still-open ISS-0680/GH-722 (resolve() leaking allocator-owned PinnedVersion fields on early error returns), NOT a symptom of the double-free this issue tracks, and out of scope for this fix per the routing handoff.
prevention: applyPinOverrides() should allocator.dupe(u8, version) (and resolved_id, if not already allocator-owned in all call paths) before calling applyOverrideToPins(), and free the ORIGINAL p.version/p.resolved_id being replaced -- mirroring the dupe-then-free pattern resolve()'s own Step 6 loop already uses for the non-override path. Alternatively, track field provenance (JSON-owned vs allocator-owned) explicitly so the Step 6 cleanup loop only frees what it actually allocated.

When a function stores a caller-scope pointer (a JSON-parsed field, a request-scoped buffer) into a struct whose lifetime and cleanup discipline is owned by a DIFFERENT, longer-lived scope, verify explicitly which allocator produced the pointer before it crosses that boundary -- do not assume 'it's a []const u8 field on this struct, so it's allocator-owned' just because sibling fields on the same struct happen to be.
